title: Getting Started
lines: **Play your music**
Press {menu} to open the menu.
Open Library, choose Local Music, open a folder, then select a track.
**Enjoy the visualizer**
Close the menu after playback starts.
Use Presets to choose a visual style and Settings to choose frame rate and resolution behavior.
The footer always shows the actions available for the current selection.

children.title: In the menu
lines: **Navigation**
{move} moves the selection. Hold to scroll faster.
{focus} switches panels.
{select} opens the selected item or applies a value.
{back} goes back or cancels editing.
Escape goes back in the menu and does nothing when it is closed. Q does not quit; close the desktop window to exit.
{pages} switches pages.
**Menu**
{menu} opens or closes the menu.
The footer shows actions for the current selection.
With a mouse or touchscreen, links in the right panel are underlined and open in your browser when selected.
Right-click or long-press a value in the right panel to copy it.
With a mouse, drag the volume value in the player bar. Without a mouse, output stays at maximum for hardware volume controls.

children.title: While listening
lines: **With the menu closed**
{tracks} selects the previous / next track.
Next respects the selected shuffle mode.
{play} plays or pauses.
{seek} seeks backward or forward.
{presets} changes the visualizer preset.
{random} chooses a random preset.
{overlay} shows or hides track notifications.

children.title: Help navigation
lines: Choose a topic on the left.
{select} opens a topic with subtopics.
{focus} moves to the text panel.
{move} scrolls the text.
{back} returns to the previous level.
{pages} returns to another application page.

children.title: Shuffle and repeat
lines: Off: tracks play in order.
Album: shuffle the current folder or playlist.
Source: shuffle within Local Music, Modland or ModArchive.
All: shuffle across available sources. Offline, All uses local music and downloaded remote tracks.
Source and All can repeat tracks, including the current track.
Repeat One repeats the current track when it ends. Manual Next still moves on.
A failed load is skipped. Repeated failures stop automatic recovery.

children.title: Seeking
lines: {seek} moves through the current track.
Tracker audio is prepared for accurate seeking when enough memory is available.
The preparation budget is selected automatically from currently available memory.
Long tracks or low-memory conditions use native streaming instead.
Backward seeking then depends on the decoder.

children.title: Favorites
lines: Select a local track, catalog track or radio station outside Favorites playlists and follow the Favorite hint in the footer.
A short press cycles Star / Heart / Note / None.
The station details show its Favorite playlist, and a badge marks saved stations in the list.
{gamepad_heading}
Hold {favourite} to remove the selected track from favorites.
Outside track browsing, {play} is Play / Pause.
{keyboard_heading}
F cycles the favorite; Delete removes it. Saved radio stations remain available after restart.

children.title: Visualizer settings
lines: Frame rate selects a fixed cap below the active display refresh, or Max (the active refresh rate).
Adaptive resolution lowers or restores the image size to approach that target.
Resolution is the maximum size when adaptation is on, and the fixed size when it is off.
Upscale filter controls the final image: Bilinear is smooth, while Nearest neighbor keeps crisp pixel edges.
Max is shown with the active refresh rate, and an equal numeric cap is hidden to avoid duplication.
If the preset is too complex even at the smallest step, the actual FPS may remain below the target.

children.title: Music without visualization
lines: Set Visualizer to Off in Settings.
Music and menu navigation keep working against a plain background.
Opening Presets still enables its live preview.
Turn Visualizer back On to resume the animation.

children.title: Preset selection
lines: Open Presets and browse the list.
Pause on a preset to see its preview.
{select} selects it; it is applied when you leave the page.
Preset auto-switch controls automatic changes.
Successful resolutions are remembered during the current run.

children.title: No music listed
lines: Open Library, choose Local Music, then select a folder containing supported audio files.
An empty folder and a failed scan are different states; check any error shown.
Downloaded catalog indexes list music, but do not contain the audio itself.

children.title: Offline catalogs
lines: Saved catalog indexes remain browsable without internet.
A track must already be downloaded to play offline.
Offline Shuffle All uses local music and downloaded remote tracks; Shuffle Source uses only cached tracks from that source. Network availability is checked periodically.

children.title: Loading or skipped tracks
lines: Downloading fetches a remote file. Preparing audio decodes a tracker for seeking.
You can select another track while loading.
Unsupported, damaged or unavailable tracks are skipped automatically.
If repeated failures stop playback, choose another track or source.

children.title: Limited seeking
lines: Some native tracker decoders cannot seek backward reliably.
Tracker seeking is prepared automatically when enough memory is available.
Very long tracks and low-memory conditions use native streaming.

children.title: Local Music
lines: **Play local files**
Browse folders on the device and play supported audio and tracker files.
Playback works without a network connection.

children.title: Favorites
lines: **Keep tracks close**
Select a local track, catalog track or radio station, then use the Favorite action shown in the footer.
A short press cycles Star, Heart, Note and no mark. Favorites are available from Library after restart.
Favorite downloads are protected from automatic cleanup.

children.title: Downloads
lines: **Offline copies**
Library > Downloads shows tracks fetched from Modland and ModArchive.
Files are stored beside the application in .cache/modland/files and .cache/modarchive/files; you do not need to move or organize them manually.
Downloaded tracks play without internet and can be removed from the Downloads view. Cache size and lifetime are configured in Settings.
Mark a downloaded track as a Favorite to protect it from automatic cleanup.

children.title: Microphone
lines: **Live input**
Select a system microphone to feed live audio into the visualizer.
Microphone capture stops track playback and is not sent to the speakers.

children.title: Radio
lines: **Internet radio**
Browse popular stations or filter by tag or country.

Recently played keeps the last 50 stations whose streams started successfully, with the start time. Unavailable stations stay in history and show a playback error; choose Clear history to empty the list. Favorite a station to keep it in a playlist after restart.
Station lists are cached for 30 days and load more rows as you scroll.
Radio needs a network connection; a stream can fail even when the directory is online.

children.title: Modland
lines: **Catalog on this device**
Playable tracks: {modland_tracks}
Folders: {modland_directories}
Network: {network_status}
**About Modland**
A large preservation archive of tracker, chiptune and game music organized by format and author.
GlitchScope keeps a compact index locally and downloads a selected track before playback.
Downloads are available offline. Mark a track as any Favorite to protect its download from automatic cleanup.

children.title: ModArchive
lines: **Catalog on this device**
Playable tracks: {modarchive_tracks}
Folders: {modarchive_directories}
Network: {network_status}
**About The Mod Archive**
A community archive dedicated to playable music modules, with artists, ratings, reviews and historical collections.
GlitchScope ships compact indexes for the historical snapshot and addendum, then downloads only the selected module data.
Downloads are available offline. Mark a track as any Favorite to protect its download from automatic cleanup.

children.title: .aac
lines: AAC is a lossy audio coding format commonly stored as raw AAC or in MP4-family containers. GlitchScope decodes it with FFmpeg.

children.title: .ac3
lines: AC-3 (Dolby Digital) is a lossy audio coding format used for mono and multichannel sound. GlitchScope decodes it with FFmpeg.

children.title: .eac3
lines: E-AC-3 (Dolby Digital Plus) extends AC-3 with higher bitrates and additional channel configurations. GlitchScope decodes it with FFmpeg.

children.title: .mp1
lines: MP1 is MPEG Audio Layer I, the earliest of the three MPEG-1 audio layers. GlitchScope decodes it with FFmpeg.

children.title: .mp2
lines: MP2 is MPEG Audio Layer II, a lossy format still encountered in broadcast and older media. GlitchScope decodes it with FFmpeg.

children.title: .mp3
lines: MP3 is MPEG Audio Layer III, a widely used lossy audio format. GlitchScope decodes it with FFmpeg.

children.title: .ogg
lines: Ogg is a container that commonly carries Vorbis, Opus, FLAC or Speex audio. GlitchScope decodes its audio stream with FFmpeg.

children.title: .oga
lines: OGA is the audio-oriented filename extension for an Ogg container. GlitchScope decodes its audio stream with FFmpeg.

children.title: .opus
lines: Opus is an open, low-delay lossy audio format standardized by the IETF. GlitchScope decodes it with FFmpeg.

children.title: .spx
lines: SPX normally contains Speex speech audio in an Ogg container. GlitchScope decodes it with FFmpeg.

children.title: .flac
lines: FLAC is an open lossless audio format that reconstructs the original PCM samples exactly. GlitchScope decodes it with FFmpeg.

children.title: .wav
lines: WAV is a RIFF-based audio container, most often used for PCM but capable of carrying other codecs. GlitchScope decodes it with FFmpeg.

children.title: .rf64
lines: RF64 extends WAV for files that exceed the classic RIFF 4 GiB size limit. GlitchScope decodes it with FFmpeg.

children.title: .aiff
lines: AIFF is Apple's IFF-based audio container, commonly used for uncompressed PCM. GlitchScope decodes it with FFmpeg.

children.title: .aif

children.title: .aifc

children.title: .caf

children.title: .m4a

children.title: .m4b

children.title: .mp4

lines: AY stores ZX Spectrum or Amstrad CPC music as Z80 program data for AY-family sound hardware. GlitchScope plays it with Game Music Emu.

lines: NSF stores Nintendo NES or Famicom music code and data for emulated playback. GlitchScope plays it with Game Music Emu.

children.title: .nsfe
lines: NSFE is an extensible NSF variant with chunked metadata and playlist information. GlitchScope plays it with Game Music Emu.

children.title: .spc
lines: SPC is a snapshot of the Super Nintendo or Super Famicom audio subsystem. GlitchScope plays it with Game Music Emu.

title: About
lines: **GlitchScope**
A music player and real-time MilkDrop visualizer built for Linux handhelds and desktop computers.
Play local audio, tracker modules and classic game-music formats, or explore the Modland and ModArchive catalogs.
Visuals are rendered by projectM. Audio is decoded by specialized open-source engines selected for each format.
Choose a frame-rate target and an independent adaptive-resolution limit. The visualizer can also be disabled for music-only playback.
